journal_entries: First memory of Half Breed; Wayward Husk that is found within Scuttling Void. Covering birth or childhood? Set up themes that will run throughout rest of memories, though moderated. Show Namira/Last king influence on birth. Birth up until puberty has boy appear as a normal Breton as per racial biology in TES, then during puberty does boy start looking like Orc. Then real story begins.

objectives: Talk to the Undertaker for work
Talk to the Priest of the Nine for work

journal_entries: Second memory portrays tumultuous puberty and changing of behavior of peers toward MC. Violent interactions with father and brothers, older brother stays away from home, only returning to get money for skooma and antagonize MC for looking like Orc. Younger brother suffered brain injury earlier in life when grandfather attempted to kill MC and his younger brother to wash away "Orc stain" from family legacy - happened when MC mother left home because violent Orc father event. Went to live with her father (Breton). Orc father only wanted normal family that wouldn't suffer stigma of being Orcs, hatred for MC stems from self-hatred. Near end of this quest there is a pogrom that has MC escape Wayrest (where they lived).

MC becomes nomadic with younger brother, escorting him due to his (brother) mental impairment. Come across Orc hunters, slavers and Ustase. Violent altercations ensue. They happen upon an Orc enclave, MC learns how to defend himself and gets into conflict with other young Orcs who know of his racial background. Eventually enclave is raided and MC, along with other Orcs, are sent to slave camps/Quarry. Eventually MC escapes slave camp after immense violence and Bretons (Ustase) maiming him; having cut part of his genitalia (will play into further themes).

Time passes as MC still escorts younger brother, physically exhausted and frustrated after all the violence and being hunted. Scene where MC takes out frustration on younger brother only to recoil and evaluate what he's doing, and where they're going. They happen upon rumors of Munstor, MC finds that there's not much choice in High Rock except there. This memory will be dedicated mostly to Munstor and what transpires there. After it all, leader of Munstor is burned in center of town where the "life-trees" were, MC gets hands chopped off and left to leave Munstor as a "warning" with younger brother. MC finds witch Zenalata and Witch offers to change his life and appearance on the condition of a sacrifice. MC sacrifices brother and becomes a revived Breton soldier - who was at Munstor. During scene where MC is being transformed, brief dream segment where last king and Namira talk to MC.

Memory covering MC integrating himself into Breton society, MC's mind is broken and hateful from all that happened. But MC also knows he must act accordingly as to not waste his new gift. MC has no skills except mercenary work, eventually ascends the social strata of Breton society, ingratiating himself with nobles and eventually a noble woman. Said woman is philanthropist but reveals that most of her efforts to help the poor/Orcs are just for self validation and MC sees fully the debauchery of high class society. Eventually MC joins or runs alongside Ustase? After certain amount of time, MC cannot take cruelty of the people he's with. He defects to Wayrest and abandons Ustase/Evermore? This is after being hunted by Prethathor for his betrayal. After some time there is the war between Wayrest and Evermore. Harlots trick Wayrestians and have the main gate opened, MC remembers one of the prostitutes who betrayed them, returning to Brothel later in present to murder her.

Prethathor chases MC through city as it burns down, MC thinks they escaped but is impaled by makeshift javelins Prethathor hurled through the smoke. Prethathor catches MC and tells him of special punishment for cowardly traitors. Prethathor drags MC to a healer and forces healer to make sure MC lives through Prethathor's flaying of him. MC is released after being flayed; dying, with only the healer's spell sustaining him for a few more hours. MC walks until finds zenalata again. Zenalata performs ritual to transform him again, however this time it does not go well and Ustase/Orc slavers find him. Say he's worth a lot to certain people in Rejects Respite. MC is brought to facility and dies, soul is sent to Scuttling void. MC begs Namira to make him forgot all that happened, Namira obliges and separates MC's Memory/reason from his Ego. Both manifesting as distinct entities that are the Wayward Husk and Wayward Ego.

Maybe mix this with the last memory? Have it happen at the end? If not, then have it separate. Here we have what Wayward Ego does to Damian, where Witchmen conduct a special ambush on Damian's caravan. Wayward Ego is there too but doesn't know of Witchman plan. Wayward Ego collects body of Damian to take to Witch; Zenalata.

title: DREAMS OF PEACE
journal_entries: I should see if there are any duties to take on as to fulfill my role as a Knight. Kegor should be the first point of call when it comes to burdening myself with work.

Kegor has assigned me to my first duties for the Kingdom - I'm to collect reports from around the Reach. With many locations undergoing repairs there will surely be much to note down, let's hope there isn't too much paperwork to haul around.
I've collected all the reports and should return to Kegor with the logs - lest the rainy land consumes the paper as It has everything else.

With Kegor taking the burden of the reports, he has now directed me to talk with the King in person. It's surprising that the King would trust me with his immediate requests so quickly, nevertheless I shall meet him.

King Sigmayne ordered me to escort children from Arnima , or Raven Spring as it's now known, to Evermore. The motive is to relieve The Reach of the worries of children under threat from the myriad dangers in the land - a most altruistic desire that isn't fitting for this kingdom.  I had also met the prince, and possibly a soon-to-be king - interrupting my conversation with Sigmayne. I hadn't known everyone was privy to Namira's involvement, word gets around fast I guess....

King Sigmayne ordered me to escort children from Arnima , or Raven Spring as it's now known, to Evermore. The motive is to relieve the Reach of the worries of children under threat from the myriad dangers in the land - a most altruistic desire that isn't fitting for this kingdom.

The Archbishop has taken the children off my hands to escort them on the final stretch of their journey to some unknown destination. He had also informed me of a speech taking place within the city, by an Orc no less. I follow my curiosity without question to see this display.
objectives: See how the DeepCrag Ravine outpost is fairing
See how the people of the Bog are doing
See how the people of Lonely Griffon's Retreat are doing.
Inform Kegor about what happend at Griffon's Retreat
See Kegor about your retrieval of the logs.
Go to Arnima to escort the children.
See what the Arch Priest was talking about

title: Periphery
journal_entries: The Orc was already midway through his speech, I should stay and listen to what else he has to say.
A shriek was heard from the brothel which had alerted myself and Kegor, I follow Kegor to the brothel to discern what has transpired.
A macabre sight blinds us to the otherwise beautiful brothel - aghast and confused, I rely on Kegor to give some insight.
Kegor told me to investigate the sewers for any traces of the murderer, no doubt whatever could be found in these damp tunnels would be washed away or mixed with the filth.

I had found a second victim who was brutally deprived of her life in this wretched sewer. Amongst the abhorrent scene was a small piece of flesh, carved from the victim, bearing an etched symbol. With nothing else, I will return to Kegor with this morsel of evidence. If possible, I should see if the beggars had seen the killer as well.

A beggar had remarked on seeing the suspect escaping through their "home", she detailed his appearance "Covered in blood, with a golden shine to the hair". Could this be the work of some deranged Nord? Witchman? The answer will forever elude me if this evidence is the only thing to go on.

I've shown the vile scrap of flesh to Kegor; recoiling, he then delved into thought - tasking me with tracking down the source of the killer through the skills of the missionary in Raven Spring. I knew the missionary could trace the location of items directly, but never to this extent. I head toward Raven Spring yet again.
I should wait for the missionary to perform the search, which may take a day - in the meantime I can attend to any other tasks left pending.
The missionary should have completed the search by now, only one way to be sure and that's to speak with him.

Rejects Respite: an abandoned facility in the mountains that the Missionary had traced the source of the killers imprint to. I'm not sure what to expect there, but as always I will prepare for the worst. I've also received a staff [Staff of the Farseer] that may be of use within the dark sanctum.
The staff had opened access to the deepest bowels of this facility, it's now incumbent on me to search every nook and cranny -  was the knighthood really worth this trouble I wonder?

I still live, but in the same condition as I had before whatever just happened, I'm not sure. Some psychic force had overwhelmed my senses leading to me blacking out from the cacophony of noise, real and unreal. With the way I entered this place now blocked, there's only one way forward - deeper.

I see a light against the background of deep black and hear the ethereal, yet comforting voice of Mara - I probably have no other choice except to follow her. This surreal and unnerving experience must have an end, I'm not sure if my sanity can remain intact.

That same feeling of dread and futility, that same suffocating stench - this very same world I had entered after Mortifayne's undoing. I thought I had closed the fissure to this evil realm after displacing the sigil stone, I thought wrong. Though something is different, this realm has become dimmer, and the scenery shifts and churns even more frantically than it did before - as though its desperately clinging onto stability.
Hesitant to move any further, logic overrides my trepidation to state "There is no way back". So I follow this ominous entity, and try to glean what its motives are.

Investigate the sewers for signs of the murderer.

Understand what this creature is about

title: Pathos for Perdition
journal_entries: Back in reality, I am greeted not by that pungent odor of death, but of the fresh air of Nirn. I want to savour this moment as I'm not sure what foul trick is being played - I hear voices from outside, I should see from which lips they usher.

I looked around and spoke to who I assumed was Drugo, I feel comfortable enough to deduce that I'm back in the real world. The Imperials were talking about uprooting to make way for Skyrim, leaving The Reach directly in the hands of the Bretons. Drugo also spoke of Damian speaking in Arnima - this must be a speech with some substance for him to mention it. I should make my way for the town.............. Arnima, why did I write Arnima?
Wanting a small moment of solace, the priest had assailed my desire to remind me where I am - a realm where enjoying peace must be illegal. I follow him inside the temple to hear some more bad news.

The priest seems to outdo himself with every dreadful revelation - ramping up the stakes until it has now endangered the entire Kingdom. Damian; the prince, is suspect of being possessed by some demon - at least this is what I could gather from the ramblings of the Priest. I resist the urge to sate my curiosity further, yet I know that any calamity involving the prince would have me succumb to guilt.

The same omen I interacted with in that ill-begotten realm had appeared outside the Quarry, and from the lack of concern by any who should have caught sight of him - I deduced that I must be the only one who can. This illusory figure tasked me with killing the Prince of all people, and plunging the kingdom into perdition. Am I so foolish to follow the order of demons?

I acceded to the request from Damian - to slay that Orc speaker who may inspire other Orcs and Bretons alike to forgo their ancient hatred for each other, to instead bastardize this land with their mixing. I am a loyal subject of the king, I will adhere to any and every order placed upon me, no questions asked.

I've slain Damian and most certainly damned this kingdom to turmoil and uncertainty - this grief was however drowned with disgust at this perverted scene I came across. The children I had escorted to Evermore were being used to fulfill the demented vices of these old, grubby men. I try to lead them to the surface so they may return to their families. Were it so simple - I am walking my way into the maw of chaos.

The King himself was in conspiracy to keep this cabal of deviants and their victims a secret to all his subordinates. The very roots of this kingdom seemed to have been poisoned - and I should have seen it from the start. I shirked to acknowledge all the warning signs and had just pushed on to fulfill my own needs. I pay the price for such solipsism - now the peasants revolt and an unknown kingdom lays siege to our walls.
objectives: See what's going on in Raven Spring
Follow the Priest and talk with him inside the temple
Find a way to elimate Damian or talk with him
Take the heads of the Orc diplomat and any who may guard him (<Global=ArnaMQ13HeadCount>/<Global=ArnaMQ13HeadTotal>)
Slay the King or escape the palace

title: Iris
journal_entries: Mara wept, in her manic state she had exposed herself in Namira's vile lair, I pray that she has not been defiled by her malice. She sought to return me to Nirn, and here I am - her reasoning that I could maybe salvage what little hope remains among this corrupted kingdom. I should be overwhelmed by despair at the futility of my adventures here, that it was all for naught - Yet I see a flicker, an epiphany shouting in my ear. A kingdom, nay an entire system must fall for something better to take its place, however bloody that change is.

The firstborn had sought to burn me in the rubble, with my plight forgotten among the ashes of this terrible place. I was ripped into that red realm however, I would be grateful if I had landed in any other realm,  I guess I should be happy that I still breathe. But as soon as I had went to that realm, I had left it - back to the fresh air of Nirn again - well, fresher than the dump that preceded it. Smoke from the rubble behind had made me regained the senses. Anka was there, telling me of the situation in the kingdom, or what's left of it - and that of the Firstborn. Our main priority should be to escape, but there's a whole land of chaos between us and our exit.

The kingdom has been plunged into irrevocable disorder, carnage has cleaved itself right through the land. I should seek to escape by heading east for the Divide, there seems to be little to save within this city. Maybe I'll make good on Mara's plea on my journey East.

Upon reaching the Divide, I saw the familiar, hulking figure of Horustair. Speaking to him, he let slip of an imminent danger from Orc Shamans in the swamp - mirroring the events that marked Mados' death and Grey Belmors sacking. With few men to send out to deal with this threat, he felt assured that I could succeed where the legendary Mados had failed.
The shamans fell and I had triumphed, though this victory feels hollow - like rats fighting over a dung heap. Putting aside this malaise, I return to Horustair to inform him of the success.

Horustair thanked me, and I appreciated his sincerity - he told me the Merchants are to travel East to Skyrim and Cyrodiil. If I want to leave this chaos, then I should speak with those who will make the trek yet again across that rocky maze. I don't need to note the irony - I guess the Orcs fleeing the Reach when I first arrived in this realm will have company.

Hauntology: You are hounded by phantoms from different realities - realities where things turned out better, where you were faster and could save more people. These ghosts will continue to plague your conscience as your mind cannot cope with your own reality, that which is the worst possible strand that the gods could have chosen. You have a long walk ahead of you, enough time to dwell on what happened - or not - we mortals have a surprising propensity to carry on. Yet maybe that endurance is our ultimate downfall, to forget the lessons of yesterday to have a fresh tomorrow. Even Mara dares not speak now, you see that the sun dims, and the world grows colder.
objectives: (Optional) Track down the Firstborn and confront him
Find a way out of The Reach
Search for Luther within Arnima's dungeon.
Escort the Orcs across The Divide. {Have Anka-UR follow you to destination}
Make your way across the Bridge {Have Dawn follow you to other side}
Find your own way back to Skyrim

title: Gestalt
journal_entries: My progress through the asylum was stifled by a gate that would not budge despite my efforts, at the other end of the hall is a door that leads deeper into this haunted sanctum. If I am to find a key to overcome this gate, it may be found down there.

This department of the asylum is host to madness - spawned of the malice that took place during its function. Now that madness has festered into a manifest desire to swallow all that comes within. The initial quest for that key is quickly being overcome with my need to escape. Twisted is my fate with the tangles of this realm.

Nightmare unraveled before me, yet try as I may I cannot wake from this spiral. This creature has captured me in its game, blocking the exit, leaving me no choice but to face it head on. If I am to destroy this entity, then these pulsating arteries may help in that effort. I should sever them, and then strike at the body at the middle of this bloody maw.

Through immeasurable will I emerge alive, with that evil receding to whatever dark hole from whence it spawned. I stagger from the stageroom and press onwards, downwards, to yet even greater darkness? I purge the thought, to preserve what sanity remains.
objectives: Enter the Mortal Ward to lower the gate.
Search the Mortal Ward for the key.
Acquire the key and leave the Mortal Ward.
Bring 3 Pickaxes to the Bog Overseer (<Global=ArnapickCount>/<Global=ArnapickTotal>)

title: A Dual Soul and the Wayward Witch
journal_entries: The officer was concerned about the woman we rescued from the Orcs at Deepcrag; Denze. Rightly so, he said that she vanished from the garrison to seek out a Witch in the wilderness north of Evermore. Not being able to spare any of his own men, he tasked me instead to return her.

The witch speaks in riddles and evades questions, however her rambling did reach a conclusion. She wanted me to bring her ingredients for the ritual that will take place to deprive Denize of her would-be child.

Again I beheld tragedy - the witch deceived us and took Denize's life as well as the soul of her child. I return to the officer begrudgingly, for I must again be the bearer of bad news. Denize was swallowed by the animosity and strife that precludes the relations between Orcs and Bretons, another unfortunate victim of this spiraling madness.

Using my initiative, I spoke to the Officer regarding the ingredients which then he informed me was a dark recipe for poison. When I returned to Denize I had shared this revelation with her, and through her dismay she conceded and agreed to come back to safety. Let's hope her current change of mood is permanent - and that she has the strength to raise that tragic child.
objectives: [Optional] Talk to the Officer about the situation
Return to the Officer and inform him of Denize's demise

title: Greener Pastures
journal_entries: The Merchant spoke passionately about Orsinium, desperate to seek out its location among the winding valleys that made our journey here. There was an air of insincerity, as his desires are most probably counter to those who live in our new homeland. I should seek out other Orcs in the Reach, to gain perspective on our situation here.

Thinking I was going to be among those outside my kin for the entirety of my journey, I was glad to see the tusks on the face coming towards me - yet this joy was short lived as I was told of the situation in the Reach. One of the refugees said I should head straight to militant Orc group; "Orsinium's Sons" instead of any of the Breton strongholds. Is it really that dire here for us Orcs? I should remain vigilant.
The welcome mat the Bretons laid for me was made out of the bones and blood of my Kin - seeking self preservation, I went to the Outpost the refugee spoke of.

Stuck right in the thick of it; This warchief that lead this rabble ordered me to take the head of a scout who has yet to see us staring right back at him. With no other choice and the uncertainty that the merchant who took me who will make a return trip, I am fastened to this group for the time being.
Dealing with the scout, I make my descent towards the Warchief again - commemorating the pact that should initiate me into their ranks.
Dealing with the scout, I make my descent towards the Warchief again - commemorating the pact that should initiate me into their ranks.
My talk with the Warchief was interrupted by another of our kin, alerting us to an assault from the Bretons that is minutes away. We rush towards the gate to meet these manmer head on.
objectives: Seek your kin in The Reach.
Head west and join Orsinium's Sons
Return the head to the Warchief
Return the amulet to the Warchief
Go to the gate and defend against the Breton assault

title: Descent of the Eternal Rabbit
journal_entries: Entering the ancient ruins of Umbasir, I was immediately greeted by a strange Daedric entity. It implored me to delve deeper within the ruin so that I could speak with it up close.

This faded figure wasn't at all what I was expecting from the haunting entity that hailed me when I first entered this ruin. He must be some other agent that has little to do with what I saw - which was confirmed upon speaking with him. He asked me to activate a machine at the other end of this grand hall, which will open a link to the realm of that Daedric being.
I should use the staff I found to light the fires, as per the request of that Direnni agent. With all fires lit, it will reinstate the barrier that should protect this small outpost.
All braziers have been ignited, the barrier was erected. Now I should see why this structure is so important for the Direnni to make the effort to reach.
The same Daedric entity I saw within the ruins appeared again with another task; to find the books and evoke what I see written so that I can summon this being directly.
I've interacted with both the books, from doing so the daedric figure spawned below me - after having gone through all this effort, I seek to conclude this tale by speaking with this prince.

The summoned prince spoke of a ravanous hunger that can only be appeased by knowledge - with a particular Direnni having that knowledge which this prince most desired. I was ordered to eliminate the Direnni agent and claim his secrets through his soul.
Harnessing the soul that contains the desired knowledge, I make my way back to that Daedric prince. Who knows what rewards such a being could endow me?
objectives: Attain the staff and see if it has a use
Clear the bastion of Daedra by lighting the fires
Find out what lurks within the ominous structure
Find the books which summon the prince
